artifacts.PLAN:
C2 proposal: declared job outputs

Standing and evidence. This is a scoped planning artifact, not approval of the entire comparison or admission of a harness capability. Both supplied in/ files were read whole. f82853 approves the corrected C1 contracts and explicitly defers the outputs schema. At dfcfb464841a2e8184b62ac759a2f663fca0c50b, jobs.json contains no outputs declarations; plan, check-tests and adjudicate demand PLAN.md, SKEPTIC.md and RULING.md respectively. launch.py selects writable_out by job name on initial launch and attempts, changes Codex check-tests to workspace-write, removes snapshot write bits, and assigns out/tmp. Settlement checks read-role HEAD and residuals, with cache exclusions. Reproduction: cat ops/devlane/task/jobs.json; rg -n 'writable_out=|check-tests|TMPDIR|chmod|def _settle|_is_cache_residual' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py; sed -n '1658,1705p' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py. These are source observations, not containment measurements.

Boundary. Task owns the outputs vocabulary and its validation. Dispatch launch.py alone resolves declarations, computes grants, invokes adapters, re-admits resumes and checks output custody at settlement. record.py owns record validation. Harness adapters translate admitted grants into mechanisms; they cannot expand grants or choose policy. dispatch/go/ladder consume this execution path. Keep the permanent dev lane independent of Symfony. There is no fileset, discovery, alternative runner or lane-policy implementation in this slice.

Exact proposed schema. An optional outputs member on a harness job has the following standalone JSON Schema. Omission means an empty list and no additional worker output grant. Explicit null is invalid. A file entry is always a required, non-empty document deliverable; a scratch entry authorizes temporary work and creates no envelope artifact requirement.
{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"array","uniqueItems":true,"items":{"oneOf":[{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"const":"file"},"path":{"$ref":"#/$defs/path"},"artifact":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$","maxLength":64}},"required":["kind","path","artifact"],"additionalProperties":false},{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"const":"scratch"},"path":{"$ref":"#/$defs/path"}},"required":["kind","path"],"additionalProperties":false}]},"$defs":{"path":{"type":"string","maxLength":240,"pattern":"^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$"}}}

Additional semantic rules are normative: paths are case-sensitive POSIX-relative names beneath this job's canonical out directory, never templates or shell expressions. Reject duplicate paths even when entries differ, repeated artifact keys, ancestor/descendant overlaps, and more than one scratch entry. Reject paths colliding with adapter/launcher transport files, including the current out/last-message.json and out/COMMIT_MSG. The restricted grammar intentionally excludes absolute paths, dot segments, backslashes, whitespace, globs and substitutions. Unsupported filesystem naming or alias behavior refuses rather than normalizing into a different grant. Existing output paths and their ancestors must have the declared type and must not be symlinks; document files must not be multiply linked. Lexical validation and real-path checks alone are not race-proof containment.

Proposed catalogue data, to adopt only after the contract and independent tests:
plan.outputs = [{"kind":"file","path":"PLAN.md","artifact":"plan"}]
check-tests.outputs = [{"kind":"file","path":"SKEPTIC.md","artifact":"skeptic"},{"kind":"scratch","path":"tmp"}]
adjudicate.outputs = [{"kind":"file","path":"RULING.md","artifact":"ruling"},{"kind":"scratch","path":"tmp"}]
The scratch declarations support skeptic mutation and adjudication reproductions on disposable copies. Preserve their native prompts, role=read and document destinations. Catalogue acceptance asserts these demands; runtime authorization never searches prompts or branches on these names. A differently named job with identical declarations gets identical output treatment. Plain review jobs without declarations receive no added write grant. Existing write-job commit transport remains a compatibility obligation: this document schema does not silently authorize COMMIT_MSG or turn it into a required report; the existing envelope commit transport must remain available.

Grant intersection. Let D be the write operations requested by validated file entries and scratch subtrees, R the ceiling imposed by the selected role and job custody, P the restrictions already admitted by dispatch plus any supplied accepted profile-policy restriction, and H the operations enforceable by fresh capability evidence for the selected harness, adapter, platform and launch/resume operation. The extra worker grant is G = D intersect R intersect P intersect H. Admit only when every requested operation in D survives the intersection. A declaration demands a capability; it does not confer one. Do not silently drop scratch, downgrade a required report, widen a file grant to its parent, or fall back to inline prose. Empty D produces empty G regardless of prompt text, artifact handles or job name.

For read roles, R excludes writes to the snapshot, its Git directory, in/, context/, control files, other jobs and the host. A file entry permits its declared leaf; a scratch entry permits its declared subtree. Parent-directory writes are not implicit. An adapter requiring a prepared file may have launch create an empty, safely opened leaf before execution, but acceptance still requires the worker's non-empty result. An adapter that needs broader directory rights must refuse this contract. Launcher and harness bookkeeping permissions are separate from model tool grants and cannot be inferred from outputs. TMPDIR is assigned only from a declared scratch entry; inherited temporary paths cannot add write authority.

The parallel lane/lane-boundary-20260905 track owns profile policy. C2 consumes its accepted restriction if available and requested; it defines neither profile names nor a fallback allow policy. Existing dispatch restrictions suffice for the contract work without waiting for that track. A request requiring an unavailable profile-policy decision refuses. Harness, model, role and profile remain independent selections. Require an explicit model from the caller/configuration and preserve requested-versus-observed model provenance; an unsupported selection never triggers automatic vendor/model substitution.

One attempt path and custody. Resolve declarations from the trusted launch-side job catalogue, bind their normalized value and catalogue digest into the dispatch record through record.py, and keep the resulting grant description outside worker-writable storage. Do not reload authorization from a worker-edited snapshot. Both fresh launch and resume call the same admission operation before starting a child. Resume uses the recorded declaration, rebinds relative paths beneath the verified job directory, and rechecks current restrictions, capability freshness, aliases and output types. It cannot acquire grants from a newer catalogue. A legacy record without declarations receives no extra grant; if its saved session would retain an unrecorded grant, refuse resume and require a fresh dispatch. Re-admission must precede clearing attempt markers or restoring writable session state. Close/recovery use the same output acceptance check as normal settlement.

Acceptance. For every file entry, artifacts[artifact] must be a bounded single-line handle resolving to that declared regular, non-empty file under the bound out directory. Other existing evidence handles remain references and never authorize writes. Verify output type, containment and links without following an escape; record the accepted file digest and attempt custody. A previous attempt's report is not automatically evidence of completion: preserve it as prior evidence and require production or explicit verified reuse in the current attempt. Scratch is not a substitute report and is never auto-published. Missing output, wrong handle, unsafe output or unreadable evidence prevents status=ok. Preserve task/envelope.py as the semantic authority; do not duplicate counts/status/handle rules in a new output validator. C1's existing semantic-validator and optional commit-transport mismatch remains a named integration dependency, not a defect this contract-only bucket claims to fix.

Retain read-role source settlement in addition to output checks. Output success cannot override changed HEAD or snapshot residue. Current Git/cache-filter checks do not establish byte-for-byte immutability, detect all metadata changes, or prove that a temporary write never occurred. The prevention witness must protect source throughout execution; any stronger settlement witness needs independently specified coverage. Do not relabel chmod or a clean final Git diff as prevention.

Refusals. All admission refusals are non-overridable and carry expected, found and needed. Preserve dispatch's currently documented exit 3 and stderr refusal form in this bounded slice; founding-wire reconciliation remains separate.
- outputs-schema: expected a valid declaration with unique, non-overlapping entries; found the precise invalid member; needed correction in the trusted job catalogue. Before minting filesystem state.
- outputs-path: expected a canonical, correctly typed, unaliased target beneath this job's out; found the offending path/type/link or unavailable check; needed a fresh safe job directory or corrected declaration. Before child execution; never repair an unsafe path by following it.
- outputs-policy: expected every declared operation to survive role and admitted policy restrictions; found the excluded operation or unavailable requested policy decision; needed compatible scope or accepted policy evidence.
- output-capability: expected a fresh witness and verified mock for output writing together with retained source isolation on this operation; found unsupported, stale, failed or unobserved capability; needed a passing witness or an explicitly selected admitted harness. No approval prompt or sandbox bypass fallback.
- outputs-resume: expected a trustworthy recorded declaration and reproducible grant; found absent custody, unbounded inherited permission or changed incompatible evidence; needed a fresh dispatch or restored verifiable custody.
At settlement, outputs-missing, outputs-handle and outputs-custody identify the corresponding expected/found/needed failure in an invalid envelope with null verdict. Existing tripped outcomes retain their class and partial evidence and can never approve.

Per-harness evidence. Local reads returned codex-cli 0.153.4, Claude Code 2.1.260 and Grok 1.0.13. Commands: codex --version; codex --help; codex exec --help; codex exec resume --help; claude --version; claude --help; grok --version; grok --help. Codex help exposes sandbox modes and additional writable directories; resume help does not advertise --sandbox. OpenAI's configuration reference describes writable_roots as additional roots in workspace-write mode, not a selective read-only exception: [Configuration Reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference). Official permissions documentation describes named filesystem profiles with read/write entries and path precedence: [Permissions](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions). This is a candidate translation mechanism, not proof that the installed build enforces exact file creation, source protection, all tools and resume under the lane environment. No CLI invocation/configuration for that mechanism is admitted here.

Claude's current acceptEdits/add-dir/tool rules and Grok's current always-approve invocation do not demonstrate source-write prevention. Grok help advertises a sandbox profile option, but no suitable profile or enforcement witness was inspected. For all three harnesses, C2 capability standing in this review is unresolved: refuse capability-dependent execution until independently proved. No model/vendor execution, sandbox probe or session-store inspection ran. CLI help and mocked argv tests establish syntax/mechanics only; they cannot certify containment.

Independent tests to commission after contract admission. The test producer must be distinct from the implementation producer, with independent skeptic and final review. Name these prospective files without authoring them here:

Red basis at this ref: no declaration schema or native catalogue entries exists. Missing-symbol failures alone are not adequate behavioral reds.
- ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_launch_outputs.py: a synthetic capability counterparty proves exact intersection; contradictory prompt prose cannot grant; partial/stale/unsupported capability prevents Popen; declared outputs succeed with unchanged source; absent, forged and linked outputs invalidate; launch/resume/close share custody; catalogue changes cannot widen resume grants; explicit model selection survives unchanged. Red basis: current job-name selection, absent output admission/settlement and live-catalogue resume lookup. Mock all vendors and use disposable repositories.
- ops/devlane/harness/tests/test_output_capability.py: independently specified positive and negative probe controls, stamped per harness/version/platform/operation. Exercise direct tools and shell/subprocess writes, rename/delete, chmod-then-write, Git mutation, source-linked paths, undeclared siblings and temporary paths. A write-then-restore control distinguishes prevention from acceptance detection. Unattempted or unreachable controls are unresolved/INVALID, never passing evidence. This future probe work requires its own authorized execution environment; it is not authorized by this review.
Preserve regression coverage in test_launch_skeptic_write.py, test_launch_snapshot.py, test_launch_refusals.py, test_launch_record_paths.py and test_launch_verbs.py. Existing sandbox-label assertions need independent reconciliation with the accepted contract rather than preservation of a particular flag as the security oracle. Run ops/bin/suites.sh at subsequent landing; it was not run here because it creates temporary files and this job is read-only.

First-run walkthrough. The next worker receives the accepted C1 contracts, f82853 and this inline plan through in/. It writes only the two contract files named below in its separately authorized worker run. Its isolated home supplies no assumed operator tools/settings; missing tools or evidence are named, not fetched. A skeptic needing mutable fixtures copies them into declared scratch; tests that require editing the source, writing .git, downloading dependencies or reaching the self-hosted runner's outer workspace cannot improvise those permissions and must report the unavailable capability.
